title: The first native speaker of modern Hebrew was born in 1882
body: After spoken Mishnaic Hebrew died out in the 2nd century CE, Hebrew was nobody’s mother tongue for some 1,700 years. It lived on in prayer, scripture, scholarship and official writing, but no child grew up speaking it at home. In the 1880s Eliezer Ben-Yehuda set out to change that, raising his son Itamar Ben-Avi, born in Jerusalem on **31 July 1882**, in Hebrew; the boy became the first native speaker of the modern language. The first Hebrew kindergarten opened in 1898, and today the language has several million native speakers, something no other sacred language has achieved.

events.text: Spoken Hebrew ends as a mother tongue
Itamar Ben-Avi is born in Jerusalem
The first Hebrew kindergarten opens in Rishon LeZion
The census counts 80,396 Hebrew speakers in Palestine

slides.question: How many Hebrew speakers did the 1922 census of Palestine count?
slides.explanation: 80,396, forty years after the first native speaker was born. The Mandate made Hebrew an official language alongside English and Arabic.

slides.label: Hebrew speakers counted in the 1922 census of Mandatory Palestine
slides.text: Today several million people speak Hebrew as their mother tongue.

slides.question: In 1948, out of 10 Jews born in Palestine, how many spoke Hebrew as their only daily language?
slides.explanation: 80.9% in 1948, so eight in ten. The 1922 census had counted only 80,396 Hebrew speakers in all of Palestine.

slides.heading: A language on hold
slides.text: Hebrew never vanished. For seventeen centuries it was read, written and prayed in, and it served as a literary and official language. What it lacked was children who learned it first, and that is exactly what the revival set out to create.
